projects.name: Green Hydrogen to E-Methanol & Polypropylene Plant
projects.description:
The project involves the construction of a commercial-scale green hydrogen to e-methanol and polypropylene plant in Abu Dhabi. The project will convert green hydrogen and CO2 into e-methanol. Subsequently, the e-methanol will be transformed into propylene and polypropylene, enabling the production of these essential materials using sustainable means.

By creating this facility, the project aims to harness the power of green hydrogen and its derivatives to support industrial development and foster economic growth. Simultaneously, this initiative will play a crucial role in curbing harmful emissions, contributing to global decarbonization efforts.

This endeavor aligns perfectly with Abu Dhabi's long-term commitment to sustainable practices, emphasizing the region's dedication to environmental stewardship and promoting clean technologies. It is poised to become a vital component of the core business activities in the area, unlocking new possibilities and driving progress toward a greener and more sustainable future.

projects.name: Food Logistics Hub
projects.description:
The Dubai Global Food Logistics Hub is a planned infrastructure development initiated through an agreement between Dubai Municipality and DP World, announced in July 2024. The project involves the expansion of the existing fruit and vegetable market in Dubai to create what is intended to be the largest food logistics hub globally. It forms part of the broader Dubai Economic Agenda (D33) and aims to support national food security objectives by improving the efficiency and capacity of food trade and distribution.

The facility will include temperature-controlled storage, automated sorting and packaging systems, and integrated logistics services for import, export, and local distribution. Additional features will comprise customs processing areas, business and administrative offices, quality control laboratories, and sustainability measures such as energy-efficient infrastructure and recycling systems. The hub will be directly connected to key transport routes, including Jebel Ali Port and Al Maktoum International Airport, to facilitate regional and international trade. projects.name: PE Film Recycling Facility - Al Sajaa
projects.description:
The project involves the construction of the Middle East’s first polyethylene (PE) film recycling facility within BEEAH’s integrated waste management complex in Al Sajaa, Sharjah. The facility will focus on the sustainable management of PE film, a lightweight plastic commonly used in protective packaging and labels, which is challenging to recycle and often ends up in natural environments.

The plant will process over 7,000 tonnes of plastic waste annually, converting hard-to-recycle PE films from municipal and commercial waste into durable, reusable boards. These boards, produced through an advanced chemical-free process, will serve as an eco-friendly alternative to plywood in construction projects. The recycled boards can be reused multiple times and, once their shelf life is complete, can be reprocessed into new boards, promoting a fully circular recycling system.

This initiative will support the development of green infrastructure, reduce landfill dependency, and enhance resource efficiency. It aligns with BEEAH’s vision for achieving zero-waste cities and reinforces its leadership in resource recovery and innovation across the UAE and beyond.

projects.name: Smart Agritech Hub - Al Ain
projects.description:
The project involves the construction of a 100,000 square meter Smart Agritech Hub in Al Ain. This advanced agritech facility will integrate the latest agricultural innovations, including artificial intelligence, robotics, and sustainable practices tailored to the UAE’s unique climate.

The hub will feature SVG’s renowned “Shouguang Model” of greenhouse technology, optimized for local conditions. It will include intelligent photovoltaic glass greenhouses, thin film-connected greenhouses, and large-span solar greenhouses. These facilities will be supported by a comprehensive ecosystem encompassing seedling cultivation, post-harvest processing, storage, and distribution.

The facility will be fully powered by solar energy to reduce its carbon footprint. Integrated technologies such as AI-driven climate control, automated irrigation, and robotic harvesting will optimize resource use, reducing water and fertilizer consumption by up to 30 percent. The hub will cultivate over a dozen crops—including tomatoes, cucumbers, melons, and strawberries—with enhanced traits for flavor, resilience, and productivity.

Additional components include AI laboratories, R&D zones, advanced water treatment and purification systems, mushroom cultivation areas, energy storage units, and dedicated employee accommodations. A post-harvest complex will house cold storage units, automated sorting lines, and export-ready logistics to ensure seamless distribution to both local and international markets.

The centre will enable the full manufacturing lifecycle of commercial radar satellites, including assembly, integration, testing, and preparation for launch. In addition to industrial activities, the complex will serve as a knowledge hub by supporting a national space workforce development program. Initiatives will include academic and industry collaborations, internships for Emiratis, technical lectures, industry site visits, and research partnerships with leading Abu Dhabi universities. This initiative reflects Abu Dhabi's commitment to building a sustainable, knowledge-based economy and enhancing its sovereign capabilities in space technology.

It will be developed in phases, incorporating pellet plants, smelter furnaces, direct reduction plants, and other necessary infrastructure. The complex is designed to produce low-carbon emission raw materials for steel-making, with an annual production target of 2.5 million metric tons of reduced iron in Abu Dhabi starting in 2027.

The initiative supports Japan's steel industry in its decarbonization goals, as steel production contributes to 10% of the nation's emissions. By using reduced iron in electric furnaces, instead of traditional blast furnaces, CO2 emissions can be significantly reduced. The project also integrates hydrogen for green iron production and continues carbon capture efforts, sequestering 800,000 tonnes of CO2 annually.

projects.name: Heat Exchanger Production Facility - JAFZA
projects.description:
The project involves the construction of the largest heat exchanger production facility in the GCC, located within Jebel Ali Free Zone (Jafza), Dubai. Spanning 1.2 million square feet with a built-up area of 400,000 square feet. Designed as a key production and distribution hub, the facility will enhance supply chain efficiencies by localizing production, enabling faster deliveries across the GCC, India, China, Africa, and Asia.

It will focus on manufacturing high-performance heat exchangers using natural refrigerants such as CO2 and ammonia, catering to the growing demand for energy-efficient cooling solutions, particularly in data centers where advanced thermal management is essential for optimizing operational efficiency and sustainability.

The facility will also incorporate cutting-edge technologies, including aicore smart control solutions, which dynamically optimize cooling systems to reduce energy consumption by up to 30%, and hydroBLU technology, which balances electricity and water usage to cut water consumption by up to 90%.

This development aligns with Dubai’s Operation 300bn initiative and the Dubai Economic Agenda D33, reinforcing the UAE’s position as a hub for industrial innovation and sustainable manufacturing.

This initiative represents a key milestone in ADNOC’s strategy to expand its portfolio of low-carbon energy solutions. It supports the United Arab Emirates’ broader goals to diversify its energy mix and curb greenhouse gas emissions in alignment with international climate commitments. As a flagship component of these efforts, the facility aims to establish Abu Dhabi as a global hub for the production and export of clean hydrogen derivatives.

The project highlights the rising global demand for low-carbon ammonia, increasingly recognized as a flexible energy carrier and a vital element in the transition to a more sustainable energy future. Ammonia can be used directly as a fuel or as a carrier for hydrogen, offering a viable path to decarbonize sectors such as power generation, transportation, and heavy industry.

NAIP will comprise two primary zones. The first is the Global Logistic Park situated within KEZAD’s Free Zone, which will serve as a regional supply chain hub. The second zone, located in KEZAD’s Mainland Zone, will feature an advanced Semi Knocked Down (SKD) vehicle assembly plant alongside facilities for manufacturing key automotive components and smart hardware. This part of the development is designed with future scalability in mind, supporting potential full vehicle manufacturing capabilities.

The entire project will follow a modular, scalable, and digital design approach. It will incorporate AI-driven production systems to enable an end-to-end smart manufacturing chain—from warehousing and semi-assembly to the final product roll-out. NAIP aligns with NWTN's “Made in UAE, Delivered Globally” strategy, positioning the park as a strategic base for AI-powered vehicle production and technology development.
